summary: Mikaël Bauer specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Kanazawa University under Paul Hoornaert and Noritoshi Aramaki, and earned a PhD from Harvard University, where he studied under Ryuichi Abe (attested 2010).

Mikel Burley works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Essex under Jay M. Bernstein, Jonardon Ganeri, and Brian Carr, and completed a PhD at the University of Bristol under John Peacock in 2005. He served at the University of Leeds (attested 2007–2020).
Mikio Otsuki works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. In 2007, he is attested as a research fellow at Manpuku-ji and as a professor at Hanazono University.

Mikisaburo Mori was a scholar of philosophy and Sinology who studied at Kyoto University and earned a doctorate from Osaka University in 1962. His posts included Kyoto University (~1935–1950), Osaka High School (1942), Osaka University (1950, 1966–1973), and Bukkyo University (~1973–1984).

Milman Parry was a linguist who studied at UC Berkeley (~1919–1924) and the University of Paris (~1924–1928) under Antoine Meillet (1924). He held a post at Harvard University from around 1929 to 1935.

Milton Singer was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Texas at Austin (~1930–1936) and the University of Chicago (~1936–1940), where he subsequently held a faculty post from around 1940 to 1979.
Min Ling Khenchen Tsewang Rigdzin studied under Dilgo Khyentse and Dudjom Rinpoche.
Min Thu Wun was a scholar in linguistics who studied at the University of Rangoon (~1927–1935) under Pe Maung Tin (~1931–1935) and later at the University of Oxford (~1936–1939).
Ming Mei works in Sinology and history and archaeology. She earned an MPhil at the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin, and also studied at SOAS University of London under Andrey Terentyev.

Ming-Wood Liu works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He earned a BA at the University of Hong Kong (1966–1974) and a PhD at UCLA (1974–1979) under Kenneth K. S. Ch'en and Robert C. Epp, later becoming Professor at HKU (~1979).
Mingyu Fu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Huifeng Shi (attested 2013).

Minori Nishimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at Taisho University (~1971–1976), studying under Shunkyo Katsumata and Seiren Matsunami, and held posts at the Sanko Cultural Institute (attested 2002) and Taisho University (attested 2002–2008).

Minoru Hara was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo, Harvard, and Cambridge. He held professorships at the University of Tokyo (1960–1991) and served as President of the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (1996–2006).

Minoru Kiyota was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Tokyo under Reimon Yuki, Shinsho Hanayama, Hajime Nakamura, and Akira Hirakawa, and served as Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from around 1966 to 2013.

Minton Warren was a linguist who studied at Tufts, Yale under William Dwight Whitney, and Strasbourg (Dr. phil.). He served as Associate Professor of Latin at Johns Hopkins (1879–1899), directed the American Academy in Rome (1896–1899), and became Professor at Harvard in 1899.
Minyak Kunzang Sonam studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

id: P:Minyak Rongsharwa Tubten Lek Shé Zangpo
summary: Minyak Rongsharwa Tubten Lek Shé Zangpo studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Mio Kishimoto is a scholar of Sinology and history and archaeology. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1971–1979), she held posts at Ochanomizu University (~1979–1994) and as a professor at the University of Tokyo (~1994–2007).
Mipam Chökyi Jampa studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Mipham Chokyi Lodro was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Kalu Rinpoche (1973), and taught Trinley Thaye Dorje and Ole Nydahl.
